Confirmed baseline via direct inspection: repo clean, origin/main..HEAD=0, 149O.19.5B completed/complete, HMIC-001 verified with non-blocking findings, hardcoded False ceiling unchanged, HATP production NOT READY, runtime Observed/observe/unavailable. Read the HMIC-001 v1.0 contract directly (storage topology Sec9, write safety/atomicity Sec25, active-binding Sec26, revocation Sec28, concurrency/locking Sec30, path safety Sec36) and the 149O.19.4 plan's exact Wave-C API surface (Sec9.3: _certification_transition_lock, _read_certifications, _read_certification_bindings, _append_certification_record, _write_active_binding, _write_revocation), plus existing precedents (hatp_mandatory_cutover.py's _atomic_write_json/_reject_symlink/fcntl.flock lock idiom, hatp_evidence_store.py's exclusive hard-link publication pattern) via direct source inspection. Confirmed HMIC-REQ-083 explicitly specifies the mkstemp+fsync+os.replace whole-file atomic idiom (not HSCE's hard-link scheme) for both certification files, since each is a single shared, keyed document rather than a per-artifact file. Extended src/pcae/core/hatp_mandatory_certification.py (sole production file touched) with: _certification_transition_lock (dedicated .certification-transition.lock, fcntl.flock, distinct from HMRC-001's own .cutover-transition.lock), _reject_unsafe_protected_path (HMIC-REQ-128 symlink rejection generalized to storage paths that may not yet exist, root + immediate parent + full component chain), _atomic_write_protected_json, tri-state (OK/ABSENT/MALFORMED) readers _read_certifications/_read_certification_bindings (never auto-provisioning, never lock-acquiring), explicit-ID load seams _load_certification_record/_load_active_binding plus their production, agent-readable wrappers load_certification/load_active_binding (HMIC-REQ-019: read is not write authority), and internal admin-only-caller writers _append_certification_record (create-once with byte-exact idempotent replay, conflict rejection, and a self-consistency check re-deriving certification_id from the candidate's own eight fields before persistence -- HMIC-REQ item-16), _write_active_binding (plain locked last-write-wins per HMIC-REQ-099, never compare-and-swap, never verifies the pointed record exists), and _write_revocation (monotonic field mutation per HMIC-REQ-091, never deletion, never un-revoke, idempotent identical-timestamp replay, conflict on a differing timestamp). Both on-disk files are single shared JSON documents keyed by (repository_instance_id, canonical_deployment_root) directly under HATPTrustStore.production().root -- no directory-per-repository layout, no path ever built from certification_id (HMIC-REQ-129, structurally eliminated). Preserved Stop Condition W-1 unconditionally: the module is never imported by hatp_mandatory_cutover.py, the hardcoded False readiness ceiling is byte-unchanged, and hatp_mandatory_certification.py itself remains outside the v1.0 22-file frozen subject. No validation function, is_valid/is_certified boolean, admin ceremony, or ordinary pcae CLI surface was added; every write primitive remains private, never called with HATPTrustStore.production().root anywhere in this module -- the only intended future caller is a separate Wave E admin script. Added a 56-test Wave-C suite (tests/test_phase_149o_19_5c_hmic_protected_certification_state_store.py) covering no-auto-provisioning reads, storage topology (exactly two files + lock, no per-cert path), create-once/idempotent/conflict/self-consistency-mismatch rejection, atomic-write temp-residue-free success and fsync-failure cleanup, active-binding no-implicit-latest/explicit-pointer/plain-replace semantics, revocation field-mutation/monotonicity/idempotency/conflict/no-un-revoke, symlink rejection (root, immediate parent, both files, write-time final-path symlink), non-regular-file rejection (directory, FIFO), malformed-vs-absent distinction, multi-repository/multi-deployment isolation, copy-attack (existence does not establish a binding), dedicated-lock-file identity distinct from the cutover lock, real-thread (not mocked) concurrency races for creation/binding/revocation, production-entrypoint read-only-surface confirmation, and import-side-effect-free confirmation (subprocess-isolated).
